what: Above a static floor of a bent ridge (a concave polygon split with poly-decomp) under the panel, once the panel’s top edge passes screen center three logo pieces are thrown in from the screen sides and pile up bouncing — before touching the floor they collide only with the floor and other pieces and pass through walls, after touching they also hit walls and ceiling. Piece restitution .9, friction .1, air .01, floor restitution .3, friction .8, piece width 7.5% of the panel. They can be grabbed with the mouse and thrown again
ease: Physics (matter-js — gravity 1, piece restitution .9, friction .1, air .01, floor restitution .3, friction .8, grab force .2)

options.ground: Ridge break points 「x,y」 separated by spaces (based on 1280×256, from the left) — laid at a height of 256×(width/1280) under the board. Default is the original first ridge shape
options.width: Piece width (% of panel width), default 7.5 — original tablet 10, phone 16
options.throw: For each piece, “horizontal ratio,vertical ratio,horizontal speed %,vertical speed %,spin” separated by |. These give the start position (ratio of panel size, below 0 or above 1 is outside the panel) and the throw speed (% of panel size per tick). Default is three pieces from left, right and left.
options.[data-fx-part=piece]: Piece to throw (svg graphic etc.) — data-key holds the shape’s corner points ”x,y” (on a 0~100 box, concave is fine). If absent, a rectangle

use: …
note: On phones (no hover) pieces are not picked up. Touch just scrolls the page as usual. The ridge band drawing is drawn by whichever side uses the same ground breakpoint. Re-throw the pieces when the board size changes

from.where: index.html .i-fall (three pieces — square, hexagon, pentagon — on a ridge band at each section boundary) — original index.js physics panel: Matter.Bodies.fromVertices (ground svg path sampled at 30px, isStatic, restitution .3 · friction .8) + poly-decomp 0.3.0, piece category 4 · mask 5 (floor · pieces) → once they hit the floor, they carry on to the wall
